races.name: Betvictor Steventon Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Arabian Light
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's five-year-old mare has strong Newbury form, thrives on Good ground (11/12 sim-going), and Kieran Shoemark can exploit her front-running position as the only confirmed pace-setter in this six-runner field — her chance is real, though she's technically shown here racing slightly out of her most natural lead role at OR 111.
runners_data.comment: Arabian Light shows solid recent form, a winner four starts back, and runner-up three back, plus he brings trip and going experience and a yard in good form. The blot is an unplaced effort last time out after a 32-day break — the main threat to note.

runners_data.name: Midak
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' four-year-old is at heart a prominent racer, but with Arabian Light and Oceans Four ahead of him in the pecking order for early position, he is effectively squeezed into a midfield role that doesn't suit — his sim-going record of just 3/7 and recent soft-ground form add further doubts on today's quick surface.
runners_data.comment: Midak's recent form reads modestly — fourth last time out, ninth two starts back — and he remains without a win in his last five starts. A 41-day layoff is a further concern, though finishing fourth twice in that spell shows he retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Persica
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for Richard Hannon and Sean Levey, Persica has placed repeatedly in this grade (2-5-2-4 in last five) and her sim-going record of 8/15 is solid — she needs the pace to be honestly run, and a scenario where Arabian Light bowls along unchallenged is her biggest threat.
runners_data.comment: Persica heads the field on our figures with a second last time out, and a second three starts back, showing real consistency. He has raced over today's trip and going before and returns quickly, just 15 days on; he remains without a win in his last five starts but is rarely far away.

runners_data.name: Silawi
runners_data.note: Hamad Al Jehani's six-year-old has won on Firm ground and shown a willing attitude from off the pace, but a 154-day absence and a poor run last time at 1m4f on Firm are genuine concerns — Faleh Bughanaim takes the ride and connections will want to see her reproduce her best early-season form.
runners_data.comment: Silawi won four and five starts back, adding a solid second two starts back before a below-par sixth last time out, and he arrives with trip and going experience — form that makes him a leading threat. The obvious risk is his 154-day absence since that latest run.

runners_data.name: Al Zanati
runners_data.note: William Buick's mount is a progressive three-year-old for Charlie Appleby with a striking record of 4/5 on similar going, but his natural desire to race prominently is frustrated here — forced wider and further back than he wants to be, his age (3) and the weight allowance help, but racing against instinct is a real cost at this level.
runners_data.comment: Al Zanati won three starts back and again five back, sandwiching two runner-up efforts in between — form that marks him out as a leading threat. He has trip and going experience and joins a yard in good form, though his last-time sixth is the blot to note.

runners_data.name: Oceans Four
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand's three-year-old is the most likely horse to push Arabian Light for the early lead and give this race a genuine pace — Brian Meehan's runner has headgear noted (p), and while his form figures of 131-74 show inconsistency, he is the key pace-shape variable if he decides to press for the front.
runners_data.comment: Oceans Four is hard to fancy on our figures at the foot of this field, having managed only fourth last time out, and seventh two starts back. There is ability there though — a win three starts back, and another five back — plus experience over today's trip and going, so a bold showing can't be ruled out entirely.

races.paceDynamic: Arabian Light is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Newbury over 1m2f, Kieran Shoemark can send her forward to control what should be a measured, sustainable pace with no natural rival to press her — the redistribution of Midak and Al Zanati into midfield on the map reflects that both are genuine prominent types who simply cannot all occupy the same space, and Arabian Light is most likely to actually secure the lead. Oceans Four is the other prominent runner who may try to track Arabian Light closely, but with Midak and Al Zanati effectively forced to race off the pace against their instincts, the early gallop is unlikely to be truly searching. Persica and Silawi are genuine hold-up horses who will be delivered late, but on a flat, right-handed track that does not strongly favour closers when the pace is honest rather than fierce, they need the tempo to lift materially in the home straight. This race shape — a lone, uncontested front-runner setting a controlled Good to Firm gallop — most strongly favours prominent-to-tracking types who can sit just behind Arabian Light and pounce when she tires, rather than deep hold-up horses relying on a hot pace that may never materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Track And Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Arabian Light dictates an uncontested, even pace and the race develops into a test of sustained galloping over the final three furlongs.
scenarios.body: Arabian Light bowls along in front without pressure, setting a fair but not punishing tempo, and the horse who sits closest — Oceans Four or a misplaced prominent type — strikes past her approaching the final furlong; the flat Newbury straight suits a horse who has been travelling within himself off a controlled pace rather than one needing a fast-run race to close into.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If no horse is willing to challenge Arabian Light at any stage and she produces a solo front-running display on fast ground.
scenarios.body: With zero pressure, Shoemark nurses Arabian Light through a falsely slow early tempo, builds momentum rounding the home turn, and simply outstays rivals who have been unable to wind up from too far back; the Good to Firm surface rewards her proven form at this track and trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough — perhaps through Oceans Four pressing Arabian Light — to string the field out and set up a deep finish for the closers.
scenarios.body: A genuine two-horse duel up front burns off the early pace, leaving a fast-finishing opportunity for Persica or Silawi to sweep through from the rear; Persica's recent course form and Silawi's big-field wins on similar ground make them the likeliest beneficiaries of this less likely shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Midak or Al Zanati, racing against their natural instincts from midfield, produce an unexpected headway move on the outside to challenge the principals.
scenarios.body: Racing out of role and unable to get their natural prominent position, either horse would need to produce above-form output to win from an unfamiliar position; the STYLE_FIT discounts make this the lowest-probability scenario, dependent on everything else going wrong for the principals.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Oceans Four (headgear, Tom Marquand) decides to press Arabian Light for the lead — if he does, the race shape transforms entirely and a hot pace could open the door for Persica and Silawi.

Al Zanati and Midak, both natural prominent types, will be jostling for a position they cannot both hold — monitor the early furlongs for traffic or shuffling back that effectively eliminates their chances before the race has truly begun.

Silawi's 154-day layoff is the longest absence in the field — watch the market to see if there is confidence she has been trained to peak fitness, as her hold-up style means she gets no assistance from the race shape if she is ring-rusty.

Arabian Light's controlled, uncontested lead is the defining tactical factor — if she bowls along at an even Good to Firm clip with no challenger, the race effectively becomes a one-turn time trial and the closing duo of Persica and Silawi may simply run out of race.

races.name: Pertemps Network Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Duraji
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up horse in the race, trained by Richard Hughes and lightly ridden by Finley Marsh; his best form on good ground is over shorter trips and he requires a strong pace that this race shape is unlikely to generate, making his task harder than his OR of 96 suggests.
runners_data.comment: Duraji is the highest-rated of these seven and brings experience over today's trip, returning fresh after a 32-day break. His recent form reads modestly on paper, a third two starts back the best of it, and he remains without a win in his last five — but the figures make him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Bahadur
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride on this confirmed front-runner who won over 1m4f on good at Kempton last time; his role as sole pace-setter is an asset at this trip, though his stamina at 2m½f is unproven and his trainer's recent 14-day strike rate of 0/12 tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Bahadur won three starts back and brings trip and going experience to this test, form strong enough to make him a leading threat. The blot is a modest fifth last time out, part of a string of finishes either side of that success that leaves the picture mixed.

runners_data.name: Team Player
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Ewan Whillans who has won over both soft and standard trips, wears a tongue-tie, and arrives on the back of a 21-day break with a solid 3/14 trainer strike rate; his ability to race just off the pace in a well-structured race is directly suited to this shape.
runners_data.comment: Team Player is a leading danger, having won three and four starts back, building on a third five starts back before that. He has raced over today's trip and going before, though his only blot recently is a ninth last time out.

runners_data.name: Ride The Thunder
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old has been placed in five of his last six starts over a variety of distances and goes well on good ground, with Tom Marquand who rode him to a recent third at 13f; his proximity to the lead in this shape and proven good-to-firm form make him a natural fit for Scenario A.
runners_data.comment: Ride The Thunder has been competitive of late — third two starts back, and second three back — and brings trip and going experience plus the boost of a yard in good form. The blot is a modest sixth last time out, and he remains without a win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Shrimp Shady
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's progressive stayer has won twice at 1m4f and 1m6f on good ground and is in career-best form (four wins or places from last six), but his natural front-running instincts cannot be fully expressed here — he is likely to find himself further back than ideal, which is the key tactical caveat despite his obvious ability.
runners_data.comment: Shrimp Shady's finishing figures include two wins in his last six starts — two back, and four back — but a sixth last time out leaves him with plenty to prove near the foot of these ratings. He does have trip and going experience, so there is some hope of a bold showing despite the modest recent snapshot.

runners_data.name: Baileys Khelstar
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's six-year-old is in scintillating form having won his last two starts, including over 1m6f on good at Goodwood just 10 days ago; an aggressive front-runner by nature, he will be frustrated by Bahadur's presence ahead of him and may have to settle for a position that does not suit his best racing pattern, though his fitness is not in doubt.
runners_data.comment: Baileys Khelstar arrives in good form, a winner last time out, and again two starts back, with only one finish outside the frame in his last six starts. He has trip and going experience, yet our figures rate him bottom of these seven — a tough profile to square, but that is where he sits on our book.

runners_data.name: Almuhit
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's seven-year-old showed his best form when winning over 1m6f on good and 1m8f on good, but wears a tongue-tie and his recent form string of 39-682 reflects an inconsistent profile; like Baileys Khelstar and Shrimp Shady, he is a horse who wants to race prominently but will be squeezed into a midfield berth, blunting his effectiveness.
runners_data.comment: Almuhit was runner-up last time out, though that followed an eighth two starts back, and a sixth three starts back. A third five starts back shows ability remains, and he has trip and going experience — still without a win in his last five, a fair mid-pack sort.

races.paceDynamic: Bahadur is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of seven over this 2m½f trip on good-to-firm ground at Newbury, and with William Buick in the saddle he is likely to dictate a controlled, honest gallop rather than a true test of stamina. Behind him, Team Player and Ride The Thunder are genuine prominent types who should press into the first few positions, creating a manageable but not pedestrian pace. Shrimp Shady, Baileys Khelstar, and Almuhit are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who cannot all get their preferred position in a field where Bahadur controls the head of affairs — they are mapped to midfield by necessity, not by nature, meaning the back of the field will be populated by horses racing out of role. This race shape — a single unhurried front-runner setting a sustainable pace over a stamina trip — strongly favours horses able to race handy in second or third, accelerate off a moderate tempo in the straight, and handle good-to-firm Newbury ground; deep hold-up runners face a tactical disadvantage because the pace is unlikely to be severe enough to bring them into it late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bahadur Controls, Handy Types Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Bahadur dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the race develops into a tactical affair decided in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Buick keeps Bahadur wide and balanced on the long Newbury straight, setting a pace that never truly tests the field's stamina, and those tucked just behind — Team Player, Ride The Thunder — get the perfect gun-barrel run to pounce late. Horses racing prominently but within themselves on this sound surface benefit enormously; hold-up types like Duraji face too much cover and too little late injection of pace to reel the leaders in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Eases Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the displaced prominent types — Shrimp Shady or Baileys Khelstar — push forward earlier than expected and apply genuine pressure to Bahadur from the turn.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop over this extreme trip would stretch the field and begin to expose the front-runner, opening the door for horses with genuine stamina reserves to pick up the pieces. Baileys Khelstar and Shrimp Shady, both proven over similarly testing trips and in excellent recent form, are the likeliest beneficiaries if the pace is heightened and stamina becomes the deciding factor.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Delivers Late Run
scenarios.trigger: If Bahadur sets a surprisingly strong early tempo that burns off several rivals and leaves the race to one late, sweeping effort.
scenarios.body: Duraji, the only true hold-up horse in the field, would need a genuinely strong early pace to close the gap over this trip — his best recent form over shorter at similar going suggests he is capable of a place run if conditions break right. Even so, a lone front-runner at this distance rarely sets a pace that truly suits closers, making this scenario structurally unlikely in this field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Bahadur gets an entirely uncontested lead, conserves energy perfectly, and the chasing pack misjudges its run.
scenarios.body: On good-to-firm Newbury over an extreme trip, a front-runner with Buick's judgement of pace can occasionally steal a race when rivals leave their challenge too late, particularly if those immediately behind him are racing slightly out of their comfort zone. This scenario is structurally possible but unlikely given the quality of the prominent types immediately behind and the tendency for Newbury's straight to find out any horse who has led throughout.

watchPoints.text: Bahadur's stamina over 2m½f is unproven — if he has overextended himself by the turn into the Newbury straight, Team Player and Ride The Thunder are perfectly placed to exploit any weakness in the final furlong.

Shrimp Shady and Baileys Khelstar — both natural front-runners — may instinctively push forward from the off, and any early crowding or position-jostling between them in the first half-mile could compromise their races entirely.

Duraji's chance is acutely dependent on pace; if Buick settles Bahadur into a slow-medium gallop as expected, Finley Marsh on Duraji will have too much ground to make up from his hold-up position in the straight.

Almuhit's trainer Faye Bramley has a strong recent 14-day record of 3/5 — a small but striking sample — which is worth monitoring in the betting markets despite the horse's uncertain tactical position in this race.

The going for this race is confirmed Good to Firm (not the Good declared in the race header) — a meaningful distinction over 2m½f that will test genuine stamina and may stretch the field more than a purely tactical gallop would suggest.

races.name: Hallgarten And Novum Wines Hackwood Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Binhareer
runners_data.note: Has won twice over this course and distance on good ground and arrives in fair nick for Haggas, but she is a naturally forward-going horse who will find herself racing behind her preferred slot in this field — her best form comes when bowling along in the front rank, so being held up a spot or two may blunt her finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Binhareer was sixth last time out, but a place two starts back, and a win three starts back, show much better form further back — before another sixth four back, and a third five back. He does bring trip and going experience, but two sixths in his last five starts make him hard to fully trust.

runners_data.name: Jasour
runners_data.note: Seven runs at 6f on good ground have yielded zero wins and just one placed effort, which is a damning record at this level; the hold-up style leaves him dependent on a truly run race and the controlled pace Symbol Of Honour is likely to set makes that even less probable.
runners_data.comment: Jasour's second four starts back stands out, and with trip and going experience to call on, the scope suggested by his rating of 116 makes him a leading threat. The risk is thin recent form on paper — three sixths in his last five and an unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Mitbaahy
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old with two wins on similar going but whose best work comes from the rear — here he is a genuine hold-up horse shown in midfield simply because the map has no further room at the back; at OR 104 in a Group 3 he needs the race to be run to suit, which is unlikely given the probable tempo.
runners_data.comment: Mitbaahy's form is patchy — fifth last time out, and unplaced two starts back, though a second three starts back shows he retains ability at this level. He has trip and going experience and remains without a win in his last four starts, a fair midfield profile on our figures.

runners_data.name: Noble Champion
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's four-year-old has Group-level form over 7f and is dropping back to 6f, which may sharpen his finishing effort; Kieran Shoemark rides and the horse travelled well enough in recent runs to be interesting if the front rank comes back, though his last five at 6f include a win and some eye-catching placed efforts.
runners_data.comment: Noble Champion won four starts back and brings trip and going experience to this, form that makes him one of the leading dangers. The risk is patchy form since - only ninth last time out, and a pulled-up effort three starts back.

runners_data.name: Soldier's Tree
runners_data.note: James Owen's five-year-old is remarkably consistent at this trip with three places from five runs at 6f on good or similar ground; Sean Levey can park him right on Symbol Of Honour's girth and the horse's habit of grinding out placed efforts suggests he will be thereabouts at the line.
runners_data.comment: Soldier's Tree heads these figures on the back of real consistency — three thirds and a second among his last five, plus a win four starts back. He has trip and going experience and carries the highest rating of these seven, making him clearly the one to beat, with only the wait for another success since that win worth noting.

runners_data.name: Symbol Of Honour
runners_data.note: Buick takes the ride for Appleby on the confirmed pace-setter, and despite a moderate recent form string he is well-suited to controlling matters from the front; his strong record on good ground (five wins or places in thirteen similar-going runs) and unchallenged leader status make him the pivotal tactical factor, even if his outright finishing speed may be questioned.
runners_data.comment: Symbol Of Honour's third last time out hints at a corner being turned, and with trip and going experience to call on he's included among the leading threats. The risk is the form before that — three eighths and a fifth in his four starts previous — and he remains without a win in his last five.

runners_data.name: Song Of The Clyde
runners_data.note: The three-year-old — receiving a 5lb age allowance — won over this course and trip on good ground earlier in the season and is bred to handle fast conditions; Rossa Ryan should have him positioned just off the pace naturally, and at 130lbs versus 135lbs for the older rivals this is a horse whose tactical position and weight advantage could be decisive.
runners_data.comment: Song Of The Clyde's figures include a win two starts back, and a second five back, but a seventh last time out leaves him hard to trust near the foot of these ratings. He does have trip and going experience, so a return to his sharper form of a few runs back can't be ruled out.

races.paceDynamic: Symbol Of Honour is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Soldier's Tree and Song Of The Clyde as genuine prominent types alongside him, he faces limited early pressure and can establish a comfortable, controlled tempo on good-to-firm ground at Newbury. Soldier's Tree and Song Of The Clyde will push to track him closely, creating a genuine but not frantic pace that suits horses travelling smoothly just off the speed. Binhareer and Mitbaahy are both natural front-rank or close-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply more pace in this field than positions at the front can accommodate — Soldier's Tree and Song Of The Clyde are the more likely beneficiaries of the prominent slots, with Binhareer most apt to find herself racing behind her preferred position. The race shape — an honest but unextravagant pace set by a single confirmed leader with two legitimate chasers — strongly favours horses with a prominent-to-midfield profile who travel into the race fluently and can sustain their effort over the final two furlongs rather than those reliant on a strong finish from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Symbol Of Honour Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Symbol Of Honour bowls along uncontested and sets a true but manageable tempo that suits those racing just behind him.
scenarios.body: William Buick sends Symbol Of Honour to the front unchallenged and sets fractions that make the race honest without burning the field up, allowing the leader and close pursuers to dominate; this shape rewards horses who can lock onto the pace from a prominent position and sustain their gallop through the final furlong on fast ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Soldier's Tree or Song Of The Clyde track Symbol Of Honour closely from the start and outstay the leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Symbol Of Honour sets the pace but ties up slightly close home, allowing one of his immediate pursuers — most likely the consistent Soldier's Tree or the lightly-weighted Song Of The Clyde — to pick him off; both have the form and tactical position to exploit a fractional fade from the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the front rank comes back to the field inside the final furlong, allowing a midfield horse to weave through.
scenarios.body: Noble Champion or Jasour, tracking the pace from slightly further back, finds a gap and reels in the front rank as the pace tells; this is the least-likely shape given the moderate-not-burning tempo expected, but Noble Champion's return to 6f and prior Group form keeps it live.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If something goes wrong at the start or fractions are unusually fast, creating a strong tailwind for genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A ragged start or uncharacteristically fierce early gallop collapses the front group entering the final furlong, handing Jasour or Mitbaahy a rare opportunity to finish through beaten horses; both are true hold-up types but their recent records on similar going — particularly Jasour's string of mid-teen finishes — make this a low-probability rescue scenario.

watchPoints.text: Song Of The Clyde's 5lb weight advantage over all older rivals is material in a small-field Group 3 on fast ground — watch whether Rossa Ryan exploits the prominent position it will naturally find.
Binhareer is likely to be forced to race out of her natural front-rank role; if she gets pushed wider or further back than usual at the start, discount her chance markedly.
Jasour has an alarming record of finishing mid-teens at 6f on good ground — if the pace stays honest rather than fast, the hold-up horses including Jasour have very little hope of landing a blow.

Symbol Of Honour's early jump and the position William Buick secures in the first furlong is the race-shaping moment — if he is allowed to ease into a rhythm unchallenged, the race will almost certainly be decided among those immediately tracking him.

Noble Champion's step back to 6f from recent 7f runs is worth monitoring in running — if he travels smoothly through the first half of the race rather than getting outpaced, he becomes a legitimate late threat to the front two.

races.name: Weatherbys Super Sprint Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: From Me To You
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Hannon/Dobbs, 75 days off and two consecutive seventh-place finishes on this same Good ground limit confidence; needs others to do the donkey work and the pace here is unlikely to be strong enough.
runners_data.comment: From Me To You has been well beaten in his last three starts, a sixth last time out his best effort, and returns after 75 days off wearing cheekpieces. He has raced over today's trip and going before, but sits 24th of 26 on our figures and is hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Wait Geordie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won a Goodwood 5f on Good going and placed twice more at this course and distance on similar; Ryan booked, form figures of 1-3-8-7 show she can be inconsistent, but on a day she produces her best she stays on late.
runners_data.comment: Wait Geordie won four starts back and was third three starts back, but the last two runs have been below-par in seventh and eighth. He's fresh enough having run just 16 days ago over today's trip and going before, and sits mid-pack at eighth of 26 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Bint Archange
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins from four starts at 5f on Good, William Buick takes over and this is the strongest profile in the race — high OR, tactical position behind Ballisty likely, and a trainer (Hughes) running at 4/27 over 14 days suggesting quiet confidence.
runners_data.comment: Bint Archange won last time out, one of two wins in her last four starts, backed by a leading speed figure of 92 as our top-rated on 90. The only blot is an unplaced run two starts back, but she looks the one to beat, having raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Call Me Tomorrow
runners_data.note: Unresolved style makes placement awkward; has hit the board in all four starts on Good ground but converts nothing — Hannon's yard is firing and Jason Watson stays on.
runners_data.comment: Call Me Tomorrow was runner-up two starts back, and again four starts back, but the other two runs, including last time out, ended in fifth. She is winless in her last four starts, though she has raced over today's trip and going before and sits a fair sixth of 26 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Sky Secret
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent type with a 5f win on Good for Clive Cox; 70 days off is the only query but she was a debut winner here and PJ McDonald is a strong booking — profile suits this shape very well if fit.
runners_data.comment: Sky Secret won last time out but hasn't run since, a 70-day absence to overcome, and sits well below his official mark of 85 on our figures at 70, down in 20th of 26. He has raced over today's trip and going before, but the lengthy lay-off leaves him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Vollering
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won on debut at 5f Good and was fourth on slower ground; Tom Marquand in the saddle for Archie Watson who has a blank 14-day strike rate — softer form than her mark suggests but style suits.
runners_data.comment: Vollering won four starts back but has since found no better than third, that effort coming last time out, and has raced over today's trip and going before. The stable is out of form with no winners from 22 runners lately, a concern, and she sits a moderate 13th of 26 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Ballisty
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter, blinkered, ran just seven days ago and handles Good ground (three runs on it); sets a solo gallop at his own fractions which is a genuine tactical asset, though he has yet to win in four tries and drops from 6f to 5f.
runners_data.comment: Ballisty has been placed in each of his last four starts, third on three occasions and runner-up in between, though still winless in that sequence. He races in blinkers, is fit having run just seven days ago, and sits 11th of 26 on our figures having raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Bill The Bull
runners_data.note: Prominent type with one win at 6f Good and a tongue-tie fitted; trainer Adam Kirby has a blank 14-day strike rate, and a distant eighth last time on Good gives a form anchor to question whether he's in his best form right now.
runners_data.comment: Bill The Bull won two starts back, having been third and fourth in the pair of runs before that, form that has him rated third of 26 on 87. He wears a tongue-tie and has raced over today's distance before, but a below-par eighth last time out is the main risk.

runners_data.name: Final Appeal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer, 73 days since last run is a notable concern coming into a hot sprint; has a win and a second to his name from three starts but the long absence in a competitive handicap field makes him hard to trust at a price.
runners_data.comment: Final Appeal won two starts back and was runner-up before that, useful recent form, though the sequence ended with a below-par fifth last time out. He returns after 73 days off having raced over today's distance before, and sits a respectable seventh of 26 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Leucothea
runners_data.note: Unresolved style, no runs on Good going in recent history — all form on Soft/Standard/Firm — which adds an unknown quantity, though Hannon's yard keeps churning out runners in good form.
runners_data.comment: Leucothea has been placed in all of her last three starts, runner-up twice either side of a third, though still without a win in that sequence. She rates well above her official mark of 71 at 85, and has raced over today's distance before, an interesting fifth of 26 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Nascent Star
runners_data.note: Flagged as lightly raced — only two starts, both fourths; Palmer's runner and Finley Marsh takes the ride, but without a win or a place at the sharp end the evidence base is thin for a race of this quality.
runners_data.comment: Nascent Star has finished fourth in both of his last two starts, respectable without threatening to win, and has raced over today's trip and going before. He sits down in 21st of 26 on our figures, making him hard to fancy against this level of opposition.

runners_data.name: Seathegulls
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has never finished better than fifth in three 5f starts on Good; the Moore yard is in decent form (7/18 over 14 days) but the form profile offers little encouragement in this company.
runners_data.comment: Seathegulls has been no better than fourth in his last three starts, form that leaves him without a win in that sequence, and has raced over today's trip and going before. He rates well above his official mark, at 77 against 61, sitting a competitive 14th of 26 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Courage Best
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse flagged as a fader in the finish and has posted three consecutive ninth-place finishes at 6f on Good — dropping to 5f with George Wood may not solve the late weakening pattern.
runners_data.comment: Courage Best has been well beaten in each of her last three starts, no better than seventh, and is winless in that sequence. She's fit having run just five days ago over today's trip and going before, but sits down in 22nd of 26 on our figures, hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Minster Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent type who was second over 6f on Good and fourth over 5f for Eve Johnson Houghton; lightly raced, nine days since last run, and Charles Bishop is a reliable pilot — the step back to 5f from 6f is speculative but the style fits the pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, and fourth two starts back, Minster Boy remains without a win in that sequence. He's fit having run nine days ago over today's trip and going before, and the yard is among the form horses with 8 winners from its last 31, but he sits 19th of 26 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Niewiadoma
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with a fading tendency flagged — won on debut at 5f Good but two subsequent runs produced a ninth and a 25th; the wide variance and tendency to fade in finish make her a big risk.
runners_data.comment: Niewiadoma won three starts back but the last two runs have been below-par, ninth and then unplaced most recently. She has raced over today's trip and going before, and carries a useful speed figure of 80, though the stable is currently out of form with no winners from 22 runners lately.

runners_data.name: Rollthedicebaby
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won over 6f Soft and was second over 5f Good — Sean Levey booked for Hannon, only two starts, stepping up in class; the style is perfectly suited to this pace scenario and the form reads well on similar ground.
runners_data.comment: Rollthedicebaby won last time out having been runner-up before that, solid form across her last two starts. She returns after 36 days off having raced over today's distance before, and sits a fair tenth of 26 on our figures, matching her official mark of 81.

runners_data.name: Etienne
runners_data.note: Unresolved style, lightly raced after just one run — a 6f second on Good for Richard Spencer with David Egan taking over; this is a step into a very deep end and the single data point leaves everything to the imagination.
runners_data.comment: Etienne was runner-up on his sole recent start, a promising sign from a lightly raced type, and has raced over today's trip and going before. Fit having run 23 days ago, he sits 17th of 26 on our figures, with more needed to know his true level.

runners_data.name: Angels Lane
runners_data.note: Prominent racer, debut winner over 5f Soft for Henry Candy with apprentice Laura Pearson up; going quicker than that debut win is untested and the trainer has a small operation (0/6 over 14 days), but the profile matches the shape.
runners_data.comment: Angels Lane won her only recent start, a promising if lightly raced profile, and has raced over today's distance before. She returns after 42 days off sitting a solid ninth of 26 on our figures, with more clearly needed to confirm that level.

runners_data.name: Clueisinthetitle
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Hannon/Gordon; a 3rd at 6f Good followed by a 9th at 5f Soft last time, and the step back to Good should help, but the style requires a stronger gallop than Ballisty is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Clueisinthetitle was third last time out but well beaten in ninth two starts back, leaving her without a win in that sequence. She has raced over today's trip and going before, but sits bottom of the field on our figures, making her very hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Kodi Bear Light
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a win and a second from three starts at 5f on Good for K.R. Burke (11/46 over 14 days in cracking form); 49 days off is a query but this horse's form profile is exactly right for this pace scenario and Burke's yard deserves respect.
runners_data.comment: Kodi Bear Light won two starts back and was runner-up before that, useful form either side of a below-par sixth last time out. She's rated fourth of 26 on our figures at 87, well above her official mark of 78, and has raced over today's trip and going before, marking her a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent but the field holds more front-rank types than can physically claim those positions — she is likely to find herself racing in midfield against her instincts; her 5f Good form includes a win and two thirds (5/5 on similar going) so ability is not the issue, but a compromised draw in this scenario dampens her chance.
runners_data.comment: Holi Scarlett won two starts back and was third last time out, form that outweighs a couple of below-par efforts further back in the sequence. She's fit having run just ten days ago over today's trip and going before, and sits a fair 18th of 26 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Past Passion
runners_data.note: Front-rank by nature but, with the prominent slots already contested, she is likely to be shuffled back into midfield contrary to her best form; has placed at 5f on Good twice and trainer Portman is ticking along, though her natural style being curtailed is the key negative here.
runners_data.comment: Past Passion was runner-up last time out and was placed in two of her three starts before that, though still without a win across the sequence. She's fit having run just 16 days ago over today's trip and going before, and rates well above her official mark, at 80 against 65.

runners_data.name: Seed Ya Later
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner whose three-from-four record includes a 5f win on Good, but with a hood fitted and a field that cannot accommodate all the pace horses near the front, she faces a real risk of never settling into her rhythm; Channon has a blank 14-day strike rate and Rose Dawes is a low-profile booking — the talent is real but the tactical situation is against her.
runners_data.comment: Seed Ya Later won three starts back and was runner-up four starts back, with a below-par sixth last time out the outlier in that sequence. Wearing a hood, she's rated second of 26 on our figures at 88, well above her official mark of 67.

runners_data.name: Zigazig Ah
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won over 6f Good and was second over 6f Standard for Richard Spencer; Saffie Osborne takes the ride and the horse has only raced over 6f so far — this 5f drop is unexplored, but the early-position profile is an asset in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Zigazig Ah won last time out having been runner-up before that, solid recent form across her last two starts. She has raced over today's going before, and sits a fair 16th of 26 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Holliesthedollie
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with three runs, best effort a fourth over 6f at Sandown, and apprentice Olivia Tubb up; no evidence of 5f Good effectiveness and the rear-of-field style is poorly suited to the uncontested pace on offer.
runners_data.comment: Holliesthedollie has been no better than fourth in her last three starts, including a well-beaten eighth last time out, leaving her winless in that sequence. She has raced over today's trip and going before, but sits down in 23rd of 26 on our figures, hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Devon Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with the lowest OR in the field at 44, very quick turnaround (four days since last run), and trainer Millman has another runner (Courage Best) already in the race; best effort was a third on Good at 5f but the weight of evidence points against this field.
runners_data.comment: Devon Angel was third last time out but the three runs before that were modest, including an unplaced effort, leaving her winless in that sequence. Wearing a tongue-tie and fresh having run just four days ago, she has raced over today's distance before, but sits 25th of 26 on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Ballisty is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 26-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine rival for the lead — he can bowl along at his own tempo on Good to Firm ground without being seriously pressured, creating a sustainable, rhythmic pace rather than a frantic burn-up. The genuine prominent types — Bint Archange, Sky Secret, Vollering, Bill The Bull, Final Appeal, Rollthedicebaby, and Zigazig Ah — will jostle for the handful of spots just behind the leader, and this compression pushes Holi Scarlett, Past Passion, and Seed Ya Later (all natural front-rank horses) out of their preferred positions and into midfield against their nature. With a controlled, even gallop dictated by one uncontested leader, the race will not set up for closers making up ground from the rear, as the pace is unlikely to be fierce enough to reel back those who travel sweetly in the first two or three positions. This shape is a textbook advantage for prominent racers who can sit two or three lengths off Ballisty in a good position and kick off a steady tempo — hold-up horses will find the pace insufficient to generate the gaps they need late on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Sit-And-Kick
scenarios.trigger: If Ballisty bowls along uncontested and a prominent racer slots in behind him, travels comfortably, and pounces inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Ballisty sets a controlled, sustainable gallop on the Good to Firm surface, leaving the prominent horses just off him in the best possible position to use their energy at the death; those who travel fluently in the first three lengths of the leader avoid the midfield traffic and deliver their effort on a true, uncontested line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Ballisty's recent seasoning — seven days ago — has left him sharper rather than stale, and the moderate pace he dictates is slow enough that he never fully empties his tank.
scenarios.body: With no rival pressing him, Ballisty can dictate every fraction and conserve enough energy to repel late challengers in a 5f dash on fast ground; his prominent pursuers bunch behind him and neutralise each other, giving the leader a soft passage to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrum Sorts
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners fail to fan wide enough from the gates, creating a scramble behind Ballisty that shakes out a surprise beneficiary who finds clear running.
scenarios.body: The jostle for the handful of prominent positions in a 26-runner 5f field produces checking and crowding for Bint Archange, Vollering, and their rivals, opening a run for a fresh-legged prominent horse who clears the traffic quickly; Kodi Bear Light and Angels Lane, both lightly raced and well-treated, are the types to benefit from a fortunate split.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is sharper than expected — perhaps through a fast-away Holi Scarlett or Seed Ya Later forcing their natural position despite the field — and the front group ties up in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the redistributed prominent horses to actually bust through and burn a true pace, conditions under which hold-up horses like Wait Geordie or Bint Archange (dropping back off a strong tempo) could finish through beaten rivals; however, because Holi Scarlett, Past Passion, and Seed Ya Later are likely to be outpaced for position early, a genuine strong gallop is the lowest-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Ballisty wears blinkers and runs just seven days after his last start — watch whether he jumps smartly and dictates truly, as any stumble or slow break could immediately compromise the one scenario that relies on a solo, uncontested lead.

The prominent berths directly behind Ballisty will be fiercely contested by Bint Archange, Sky Secret, Vollering, Rollthedicebaby, Zigazig Ah, and Bill The Bull — early crowding and bumping for those positions could produce interference that changes the entire race shape before the first furlong is run.
Holi Scarlett, Seed Ya Later, and Past Passion are all natural front-rank horses who are expected to be shuffled into midfield — if any of them does force their position forward from a good draw

runners_data.name: All Moonshine
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old has won three of her last five starts including back-to-back victories at Sandown at this trip, and her confirmed front-running role suits a small field on quick ground; her sim-going record reads 1 win from 5, however, and she steps up slightly in class off OR 87, which tempers confidence slightly despite her ideal tactical position.
runners_data.comment: All Moonshine won three of her last five before an unplaced effort last time, and has raced over today's trip and going before. Rated 88 and third in the field, the scoring form marks her a leading threat, with bouncing back from that blank the main risk.

runners_data.name: New Vega
runners_data.note: Simon and Ed Crisford's three-year-old returns from a 338-day absence having last been seen finishing fourth on Soft ground, but her two Good-ground runs at 7f both produced top-two finishes — crucially her best form is on going conditions matching today's, and Rossa Ryan is a strong booking for a yard operating at 6/21 in the last fortnight.
runners_data.comment: New Vega returns after 338 days off, a big layoff, and sits bottom of our rankings despite an official mark of 92. She won two starts back and has raced over today's trip and going before, but that absence and the lowest rating here make her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Tavana
runners_data.note: Sean Levey takes the ride on Edward Smyth-Osbourne's hold-up filly who drops back to 7f after a string of disappointing 8f runs on Good ground; her best form in this trip and going combination came at the start of the campaign and she has not recaptured it, with the trainer's 0/4 over the last 14 days adding little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Tavana is rated the best of this six-strong field at 91 and returns quickly, having raced over today's trip and going just 14 days ago. She is winless in her last five starts, but that leading figure makes her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Brisk Symphony
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's three-year-old is a natural prominent racer with back-to-back runner-up finishes at 7f and strong Good-ground form, making her one of the most in-form runners in the field; Rob Hornby is a solid booking and with only 129lbs she is attractively weighted, though she was beaten into second by similar rivals and may struggle to find the extra gear required to overhaul a horse dictating from the front.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up three starts back, and again two starts back, Brisk Symphony has raced over today's trip and going before. Those placed efforts came before a below-par seventh last time out, the chief concern, but the pattern marks her among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Lightning Polka
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly wears a hood and has produced her best form at 7f on Good ground — her third-place finish 14 days ago on Good going over this trip is the most recent and relevant piece of evidence; she is a true hold-up type by style, and Kieran Shoemark's record of finding gaps in small fields is an asset, though her sim-going map of 1 win from 6 comparable runs is only modest.
runners_data.comment: Lightning Polka was third last time out wearing a hood and sits second in our rankings on 91, backed by a strong speed figure of 89. Two starts back was a below-par ninth, the main risk, but she has raced over today's trip and going before and rates a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Velvet Rhythm
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly arrives on the back of a striking run of form — four wins in her last five 7f Good-ground starts — and her raw ability stands out; in practice, however, her natural desire to race prominently cannot be satisfied here with All Moonshine filling the lead, meaning she is forced to race further back than ideal, and her style-fit discount of 0.91 is a genuine drag on her prospects unless she can overcome the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Velvet Rhythm won last time out, having landed four of her last six starts, and has raced over today's trip and going before. She's only fifth of six on our figures at 76, some way below this field, but that scoring sequence means she can't be dismissed.

races.paceDynamic: All Moonshine is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Brisk Symphony as a genuine secondary prominent type to apply any pressure, she looks set to dictate from the gates at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 7f on Good to Firm ground. Brisk Symphony will track closely in second, but with no true pace rival to force the issue, the tempo is likely to be honest rather than brutal, creating a race that plays into the hands of horses who can travel up close to the pace and strike from a position of comfort. The field nominally contains more prominent-minded types than the shape can accommodate — Velvet Rhythm is a natural front-runner who has been mapped to midfield because All Moonshine fills the lead and Brisk Symphony fills the slot behind, meaning Velvet Rhythm is unlikely to secure her natural berth. This scenario — a controlled front-runner setting a measured pace with closers needing to work through traffic — overwhelmingly favours hold-up finishers with a sharp turn of foot, though the relatively small field of six means the gaps will be available; horses racing close to the pace without having to over-exert early are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Close-Home Strike
scenarios.trigger: If All Moonshine dictates an uncontested, moderate pace and the race is decided by a sustained drive from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: All Moonshine sets fractions that suit those who have settled just behind her, and Brisk Symphony, well placed throughout, has the flat-track form to challenge strongly in the closing stages; New Vega, with strong course form on similar going, travels smoothly off the pace and hits the line hard.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If All Moonshine sets too strong a pace early and ties up inside the final furlong, leaving room for late chargers.
scenarios.body: Lightning Polka and Tavana, held up at the rear, get a clean run through the field as the principals crack in the closing stages; Lightning Polka's recent third on Good ground at 7f shows she handles this trip and surface when given a target to close on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Decided Early
scenarios.trigger: If Brisk Symphony pushes All Moonshine into a genuine pace duel from the outset, making the race truly truly truly end-to-end.
scenarios.body: The pace heats up through the first half, suiting anything that can travel in the slipstream and quicken late — New Vega's two-year-old form on Good to Good ground at 7f is the standout profile for this shape; Velvet Rhythm, though displaced from her natural role, has the raw speed to capitalise if she finds a position closer than her mapped slot suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate gallop compresses the field and the race degenerates into a sprint from 2f out with no clear pace advantage.
scenarios.body: With several horses bunched together, the outcome becomes messy and positional luck plays a large part; Tavana, stepping back from 8f and yet to fully fire this term, and Lightning Polka both sit wide enough to find daylight but their recent form makes this outcome the least predictable.

watchPoints.text: All Moonshine holds the race by the throat from gate to home straight — if she is allowed to coast in front unchallenged at a controlled pace, her winning form at this trip and distance makes her very hard to pass with only six runners.

Velvet Rhythm's four wins from seven at 7f on Good ground demand respect, but watch whether Saffie Osborne can get her into a forward enough position — if she is forced to race three or four lengths further back than usual, her finishing kick from a cold start is unproven.

New Vega's 338-day absence is the single biggest risk flag in the race; watch the market move at the final show, as Crisford's horses returning from long absences can need the run but equally can come back primed — her early-race behaviour in the paddock and at the start will be telling.

Brisk Symphony has finished second in both her 7f starts on comparable going — she is consistent but has not yet demonstrated the ability to win from a prominent position when the pace is controlled and the leader is comfortable; watch whether Hornby pushes her up to apply pressure on All Moonshine or settles for a tracking role.

The going is confirmed Good to Firm for this race, quicker than the declared Good — Tavana's entire recent run of form has come on Good or Soft ground and she has yet to win on quicker, which is worth monitoring given she is already out of form.
